episode.title: UN report: The jihad’s new center of gravity

persons.name: Edmund Fitton-Brown

organizations: UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team

organizations.name: UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team
organizations.notes: 1267 report (ISIL/AQ) covers Jan-May 2026, published second week of Aug 2026; three reports a year; 10 experts each with veto; word cap ~10,700 or lower (translation into six languages); US-Russia split since 2022 politicises briefings; avoids naming 'Central Africa Province' to spare African member-state sensibilities.

organizations.name: al-Qaeda
organizations.notes: UN: 'senior leadership remains marginalized; capability and intent to conduct external operations remain unclear' — both hosts dispute 'marginalized' (centralised money flows, shura of affiliate heads, Houthi-AQAP truce). Calls affiliates 'theaters'. Beneficiary of revived state sponsorship (Iran principal; Turkey arguably).

organizations.name: Hittin Committee
organizations.notes: Al-Qaeda's Iran-based leadership council (al-Masri, Saif al-Adel, al-Maghrebi) that Zawahiri depended on; ~6-12 US-designated AQ leaders designated as based in Iran.

organizations.name: al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP)
organizations.notes: Tasked with external operations and propaganda; de facto truce with the Houthis; exploiting ungoverned space in southern Yemen after southern-secession dispute; led by Saad al-Awlaki; al-Qosi senior leader/ideologue.

organizations.name: Houthis
organizations.notes: Ceasefire with AQAP; 'new and quite menacing relationship' with al-Shabaab.

organizations.name: al-Shabaab
organizations.notes: Controls ~35-40% of Somalia; UN: shifted to more targeted/strategic operations after 2025 surge; 'maintained relations with both AQAP and the Houthis'; leader on AQ shura and 4th/5th in AQ succession per earlier UN report; may capture Mogadishu after US withdrawal from UN mission.

organizations.name: Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM)
organizations.notes: 7,000-8,000 fighters per UN (hosts: too low); joint offensive with Tuareg militias reached Bamako's doorstep and killed Mali's defence minister; expanding into Burkina Faso, Niger, Benin; received $50M UAE ransom and shares it up the network; delivers services; Mali and Burkina Faso 'failed states'.

organizations.name: al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM)
organizations.notes: 200-300 fighters, relegated to supporting JNIM; its head sits on AQ shura and dispersed the $50M; funnels money to JNIM and AQ central.

organizations.name: Islamic State Greater Sahara
organizations.notes: About a quarter of JNIM's strength; renewed fighting with JNIM over space and smuggling routes; stronger in western Niger.

organizations.name: Islamic State West Africa Province
organizations.notes: ~2,000 members; 'most active ISIL affiliate' Jan-May 2026; Lake Chad Basin HQ; threat of linking with western theatre across Niger.

organizations.name: al-Furqan office
parent_or_allies: Islamic State General Directorate of Provinces
organizations.notes: One of three key IS regional offices (with al-Karrar in Somalia and al-Sadiq for Khorasan); headed by al-Nuki until his death.

organizations.name: al-Karrar office
parent_or_allies: Islamic State General Directorate of Provinces
organizations.notes: IS regional office once crucial to IS financing; not mentioned in the report.

organizations.name: al-Sadiq office
parent_or_allies: Islamic State General Directorate of Provinces
organizations.notes: IS regional office for South/Central Asia; not mentioned in the report.

organizations.name: Islamic State General Directorate of Provinces
organizations.notes: IS 'general manager'/CEO office line-managing the regional offices; headed by al-Nuki (Nigeria) until May 2026.

organizations.name: Islamic State
organizations.notes: UN: 'at a lower ebb fettered by leadership challenges'; centre of gravity shifted to Africa; #1 Somali, #2 Nigerian; struggling in Syria (~3,000) and Iraq (hundreds); Iraqi-chauvinist identity under strain.

organizations.name: Islamic State Somalia
organizations.notes: 150-200 fighters, limited activity, no key leaders lost; led by Mumin.

organizations.name: Allied Democratic Forces
organizations.notes: Report gives rich detail but calls it ADF rather than IS Central Africa Province to avoid offending African member states.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Fitton-Brown: 'the Afghan Taliban, AQIS and the TTP form an aggressive terrorist alliance projecting violence from Afghanistan into Pakistan with the objective of capsizing the Pakistani state'; has largely suppressed ISKP as a local force.

organizations.name: al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS)
organizations.notes: UN: AQIS 'form the backbone' of groups fighting the Pakistani state; 'point of the al-Qaeda spear for external operations', explicitly tasked to work with TTP.

organizations.name: Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan
aliases: movement of the Taliban in Pakistan
organizations.notes: Staggering numbers of attack claims in Pakistan; trained alongside BLA by al-Qaeda trainers per one member state; Pakistan calls it Indian-backed (Roggio: 'insane'); historically reached ~60 miles from Islamabad and attacked GHQ Rawalpindi.

organizations.name: Balochistan Liberation Army
organizations.notes: One member state (hosts guess Pakistan) reported BLA fighters trained alongside TTP by al-Qaeda trainers in Afghanistan; hosts flag single-source claim; BLA uses suicide tactics.

organizations.name: Turkestan Islamic Party
organizations.notes: Concentrating forces in Badakhshan (camps, weapons); Syrian fighters rolled into a Syrian army unit; radicalised Uyghurs a problem in Syria/Turkey; not a huge threat to China per Fitton-Brown.

organizations.name: Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP)
organizations.notes: UN: primary threat to Taliban rule; hosts: largely contained, more a propaganda nuisance; Tajik diaspora vector for external attacks less emphasised this report.

organizations.name: Hurras al-Din
organizations.notes: UN: despite self-declared dissolution, persists through a clandestine, decentralised structure with up to 1,000 fighters.

organizations.name: Syrian government
organizations.notes: High number of foreign fighters in military/police; former al-Hol inmates joining; ISIS infiltrators killed US servicemen; 'Turkish-sponsored terror' stepped into Syria's vacuum.

organizations.name: Iranian government
organizations.notes: Principal state sponsor of al-Qaeda; hosts the Hittin Committee and Saif al-Adel; sole member state denying he is in Iran; secret AQ-Iran deal disclosed by US in 2009.

organizations.name: Government of Turkey
organizations.notes: Fitton-Brown: could now be seen as a state sponsor of al-Qaeda; sponsors Muslim Brotherhood; 'Turkish-sponsored terror' in Syria; pro-Somali-unity.

organizations.name: Government of Qatar
organizations.notes: Named as malign state sponsor alongside Turkey and Iran; not addressable in UN report mandate.

organizations.name: United Arab Emirates
organizations.notes: Paid $50 million ransom to al-Qaeda in the Sahel to free its people; pro-Somaliland.

organizations.name: Muslim Brotherhood
organizations.notes: Ideological wellspring of jihadist groups; barriers with them breaking down since 7 Oct 2023.

organizations.name: Russian Africa Corps
organizations.notes: Supports Sahel juntas; 'brutalize the citizenry and steal rare earth minerals'.

organizations.name: Somali federal government
organizations.notes: Weak, corrupt, 'probably doomed'; no control over Puntland/Somaliland.

organizations.name: Government of Pakistan
organizations.notes: Nuclear-armed state at risk of jihadist capsizing; briefs against India at the UN (and vice versa).

organizations.name: Foundation for Defense of Democracies
organizations.notes: Both hosts are senior fellows; Ahmad Sharawi reported on TIP in Syrian army.

organizations.name: Boko Haram
organizations.notes: Strong in northeastern Nigeria.

events.description: UN Monitoring Team 1267 report on ISIL and al-Qaeda published (covering Jan-May 2026): Africa main battlefield; AQ senior leadership 'marginalized'; Saif al-Adel explicitly placed in Iran; AQ-TTP collaboration in Pakistan; AQ status in Afghanistan 'unchanged'.
actors: UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team

events.description: US killed Islamic State deputy leader and GDP head Abu Maryam al-Nuki in Nigeria.
UAE paid a $50 million ransom to al-Qaeda (JNIM) in the Sahel to free its nationals; money dispersed across the al-Qaeda network including to central leadership.
JNIM joint offensive with Tuareg militias in Mali reached the doorstep of Bamako and killed Mali's defence minister.
UN report cites al-Qaeda's 'newly established training camp in Barg-i-Matal, Nuristan' and TIP concentrating forces in Badakhshan.
One member state reported BLA fighters trained alongside TTP by al-Qaeda trainers in Afghanistan.
Episode recorded on 14 Aug 2026, the day before the fifth anniversary of the fall of Kabul.
Closure of al-Hol camp in eastern Syria left tens of thousands of former inmates unaccounted for; UN says >1,000 may have joined IS and others Syrian government forces.
Israel recognised Somaliland, triggering regional competition (UAE/US/Ethiopia vs Turkey/Saudi/Qatar).
US withdrawal from the UN mission in Somalia (after the report's cut-off); Fitton-Brown fears a short road to al-Shabaab taking Mogadishu.
Death of AQAP emir Khalid Batarfi and, at about the same time, of Saif al-Adel's son in Yemen while working with AQAP.
Zawahiri killed (as Fitton-Brown left the UN); Saif al-Adel, already in Iran, became leader.
Abu Muhammad al-Masri assassinated in Iran by the Israelis; Saif al-Adel rose to #2 and al-Maghrebi to #3 (date not stated by hosts).
7 October 2023; since then an era of revived state sponsorship of terrorism and convergence of anti-Western jihadist forces incl. Muslim Brotherhood.
US government (Obama administration) disclosed a secret deal between al-Qaeda and Iran.
TTP attempted Times Square bombing after Hakimullah Mehsud was wrongly reported dead four ways in 2009-10; TTP sent Roggio the video.

Previous UN Monitoring Team reports (AQ camps in 13 provinces; Shabaab leader in AQ succession)

key_claims: The UN now states explicitly that Saif al-Adel is in Iran (only Iran dissents); the Hittin Committee has long been Iran-based, and al-Adel is converting al-Qaeda into an associate of Iran's axis of resistance (Houthi-AQAP truce, Houthi-Shabaab ties).

Both hosts reject the report's line that AQ senior leadership is 'marginalized': the $50M UAE ransom was shared up the network, affiliate heads sit on the AQ shura, and no defections or splits are visible; AQAP's al-Qosi is an ideologue, not a rival emir.

The Afghan Taliban, AQIS and TTP form an alliance projecting violence from Afghanistan to 'capsize' nuclear-armed Pakistan; AQ status in Afghanistan 'unchanged', new camp in Barg-i-Matal, TIP massing in Badakhshan, possible AQ training of the BLA.

The Islamic State's centre of gravity has shifted to Africa: a Somali caliph (Mumin) and Nigerian deputy (al-Nuki, killed May 2026); ISWAP the most active affiliate; Roggio remains skeptical Mumin is caliph.

Mali and Burkina Faso are failed states and Niger is close; JNIM (7-8k+) is capturing territory and may settle for a chokehold on the capitals; eastern and western Sahel theatres risk linking across Niger/Nigeria.
Since 7 Oct 2023 state sponsorship of jihadism (Iran, Turkey, Qatar) has revived and barriers with the Muslim Brotherhood are falling; the UN cannot say so because any of its 10 experts can veto.

Partnering with 'less aggressive' jihadists (Taliban vs ISKP, al-Sharaa vs IS) is a strategic error; Syria's vacuum is filled by Turkish-sponsored terror and Iraq's by Iranian-sponsored terror; al-Hol's closure loosed tens of thousands of IS-indoctrinated people.

Shabaab controls 35-40% of Somalia and, with the US leaving the UN mission, may soon take Mogadishu; Somalia coverage is thin because of word limits and member-state sensitivities (Somaliland recognition).
